extracted.intended_audience: early 18th-century literate readers / subscribers to The Spectator; general educated public interested in manners, rhetoric, and moral essays
extracted.subtask_description: Periodical moral essays advising readers on rhetoric, emotions (pity, modesty), self-examination, and conduct in love and friendship; guidance is framed as prescriptive observations and examples. Useful for producing or evaluating short moral/cultural essays aimed at an educated public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evoke pity by genuine emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Writer should work himself up, if possible, to the Pitch of Sorrow which he endeavours to produce in others; grief has a natural Eloquence belonging to it, and breaks out in more moving Sentiments than be supplied by the finest Imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stirring up real feeling in the writer best produces pity in readers; first-person or self-sufferings often move more than artful invention. 'There are none therefore who stir up Pity so much as those who indite their own Sufferings.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer short true speeches for emotional impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Short Speeches, or Sentences which we often meet with in Histories, make a deeper Impression on the Mind of the Reader, than the most laboured Strokes in a well-written Tragedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise, factual, authentic utterances (historical letters, plain statements) rather than long-wrought fictional description to produce stronger feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use truth/matter-of-fact rather than fiction for immediacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth and Matter of Fact sets the Person actually before us in the one, whom Fiction places at a greater Distance from us in the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aiming to move or persuade, ground writing in authentic facts or genuine testimony to create immediacy and stronger reader sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on nature/spontaneity over mere artifice when evoking passion
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature on this Occasion dictates a thousand passionate things which cannot be supplied by Art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow natural impulses and spontaneous expression to shape emotional passages; contrived artifice cannot supply the same depth of feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent erotic desire with modesty and suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Desire is corrected when there is a Tenderness or Admiration expressed which partakes the Passion. Licentious Language has something brutal in it, which disgraces Humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To depict or engage sexual/romantic feeling tastefully, use gentle art, complaisance, courtship, suggestion and modest imagery (examples: Antony's description of Cleopatra, pastorals). Avoid forward obtrusion, rustic or licentious language which offends refined taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use subtlety (the 'prevailing gentle art') rather than bluntness
rubrics_metrics.description: That prevailing gentle Art... can with a resistless Charm impart the loosest Wishes to the chastest Heart... made up of Complaisance, Courtship, and artful Conformity to the Modesty of a Woman's Manners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ attention to a beloved's modesty (soft looks, small attentions, restrained gestures) to create attraction without coarse expression; these arts are honest when motives are honest but infamous when misapplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warn readers against intimate cross-sex friendships
rubrics_metrics.description: Women may disguise it if they think fit... it is natural to them, that they have no Manner of Approbation of Men, without some Degree of Love: For this Reason he is dangerous to be entertaind as a Friend or Visitant who is capable of gaining any eminent Esteem or Observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise caution in friendships between men and women because esteem and approbation easily grow into love; intimate amity can produce fatal effects and misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not marry without genuine love
rubrics_metrics.description: To marry a Woman with the Coldness that usually indeed comes on after Marriage, is ruining one's self with one's Eyes open; besides it is really doing her an Injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid entering marriage from habit, convenience, or false assurances; breaking off a match is preferable to marrying coldly and injuring both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discover secret faults by attending to enemies' characterisations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider well what are the Characters which they bear among their Enemies... An Adversary... makes a stricter Search into us, discovers every Flaw and Imperfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the harsher picture painted by one's enemies as a diagnostic tool: enemies' reproaches often reveal real blemishes that friends and self-flattery hide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test whether public praises arise from laudable motives
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider on the other hand how far you may deserve the Praises and Approbations which the World bestow upon us: whether the Actions they celebrate proceed from laudable and worthy Motives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on motives behind admired actions; do not accept praise uncritically—determine whether virtue is genuine or merely appearance pleasing to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious about virtues of a doubtful or partisan nature
rubrics_metrics.description: We should not lay too great a Stress on any supposed Virtues we possess that are of a doubtful Nature: And such we may esteem all those in which Multitudes of Men dissent from us... Intemperate Zeal, Bigotry and Persecution... produce infinite Calamities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid elevating partisan or disputable behaviours into proofs of virtue; beware zeal and persecutory conduct even if it flatters one's in-group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspect actions directed by personal bias or interest
rubrics_metrics.description: We should likewise be very apprehensive of those Actions which proceed from natural Constitution, favourite Passions, particular Education, or whatever promotes our worldly Interest or Advantage... These are the Inlets of Prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating one's character or decisions, be alert to hidden motives (temperament, habit, self-interest) that distort judgment; treat such impulses as potential sources of error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sacred rules and an exemplar for self-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The usual Means prescribed for this Purpose, are to examine our selves by the Rules which are laid down for our Direction in Sacred Writ, and to compare our Lives with the Life of that Person who acted up to the Perfection of Human Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For moral self-assessment, compare actions against religious/ethical standards and the life of the exemplary figure (here, Christ) to reveal secret faults and guide improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess comic/wordplay (punning) in social/contextual terms
rubrics_metrics.description: This humbler Exercise [punning] may be as instrumental in diverting us from any innovating Schemes and Hypothesis in Wit, as dwelling upon honest Orthodox Logic would be in securing us from Heresie in Religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While puns are a lower form of wit (a 'mongrel miscreated' kind), they have a social function: they can divert from dangerous innovation in taste. Also note social associations (e.g., tavern habits) that explain prevalence; evaluate such wit both for its quality and its social effect.
